source.text: וְהַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיְכַסֻּ֨הוּ֙ בַּבְּגָדִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִחַ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king David [was] old, coming in the days; and they covered him with the garments, but not was warm to him.

en.L: And King David [was] old, advanced in days; and they covered him with garments, but he did not get warm.
en.B: King David was now old, well on in years. They covered him with clothes, but he could not keep warm.
en.R: King David was now very old. They covered him with clothes and blankets, but he still could not get warm.

decisions.choice: coming into the days: advanced in age
decisions.reason: To "come into the days" is a Hebrew way of saying someone is far on in life (Genesis 24:1; Joshua 13:1). David was about seventy at his death (2 Samuel 5:4).

decisions.choice: they covered him: those who looked after him
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It means the people around the king, the servants who speak in verse 2.

decisions.choice: he did not get warm: a sign of failing strength
decisions.reason: The story opens with the king's weakness. The once mighty warrior cannot keep himself warm, and this sets the scene for the struggle over who will follow him.

decisions.choice: well on in years
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English phrase for "coming into the days".

decisions.choice: clothes and blankets
decisions.reason: Readable adds "blankets" because the garments here were bedclothes laid over a man lying down, as verse 2 shows.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ עֲבָדָ֗יו יְבַקְשׁ֞וּ לַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה וְעָֽמְדָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּתְהִי־ל֖וֹ סֹכֶ֑נֶת וְשָׁכְבָ֣ה בְחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וְחַ֖ם לַאדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him his servants, let them seek for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and she will stand before the king and will be to him a caretaker, and she will lie in your bosom, and will be warm to my lord the king.

en.L: And his servants said to him, "Let them seek for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and let her stand before the king and be a caretaker to him, and let her lie in your bosom, and my lord the king will get warm."
en.B: So his officials said to him, "Let a young virgin be found for my lord the king, to wait on the king and look after him. Let her lie in your arms, so that my lord the king may keep warm."
en.R: So his officials said to him, "Your Majesty, let us look for a young woman, a virgin. She can serve you and take care of you. She can lie close beside you and keep you warm."

decisions.choice: caretaker: one who looks after and tends someone
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It comes from a verb meaning "to be of use, to serve", and here it names a woman who waits on the old king and cares for him. It does not mean a wife.

decisions.choice: stand before the king: serve him
decisions.reason: To "stand before" someone of rank is to wait on him and be at his service (1 Samuel 16:21-22).

decisions.choice: lie in your bosom: lie close to keep him warm
decisions.reason: The purpose the servants give is warmth: a young person's body heat for a cold old man. The phrase can also be used of a wife (2 Samuel 12:8), but verse 4 says plainly that there were no sexual relations.

decisions.choice: my lord the king: the polite way to speak to a king
decisions.reason: Courtiers speak of the king in the third person, "my lord the king", even while speaking to him, and then switch to "you" ("your bosom"). The switch is natural in Hebrew court speech.

decisions.choice: his officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants (*'avadim*) are his court officials. As elsewhere in Samuel and Kings, Literal says "servants" and Balanced and Readable say "officials".

decisions.choice: Your Majesty; you
decisions.reason: Readable uses a modern form of address to a king and speaks to him as "you" throughout, as in 1 Samuel 17:55.

source.text: וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה יָפָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ אֶת־אֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית וַיָּבִ֥אוּ אֹתָ֖הּ לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sought a young woman beautiful in all [the] territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

en.L: And they sought a beautiful young woman in all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
en.B: So they searched throughout the land of Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag the Shunammite, and they brought her to the king.
en.R: So they looked all over Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag, from the town of Shunem, and brought her to the king.

decisions.choice: Abishag the Shunammite: a woman from Shunem
decisions.reason: Shunem was a town in the territory of Issachar, in the Jezreel valley (Joshua 19:18; 1 Samuel 28:4; 2 Kings 4:8). Abishag matters again in 2:13-25, where Adonijah asks to marry her.

decisions.choice: in all the territory of Israel: a wide search
decisions.reason: The search went through the whole land, which shows the care taken to find the most fitting young woman for the king.

decisions.choice: from the town of Shunem
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "Shunammite".

source.text: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה יָפָ֣ה עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וַתְּהִ֨י לַמֶּ֤לֶךְ סֹכֶ֨נֶת֙ וַתְּשָׁ֣רְתֵ֔הוּ וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יְדָעָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the young woman [was] beautiful to very [much], and she was to the king a caretaker, and she served him; and the king not knew her.

en.L: And the young woman [was] very beautiful; and she became a caretaker to the king and served him, but the king did not know her.
en.B: The young woman was very beautiful. She looked after the king and waited on him, but the king had no sexual relations with her.
en.R: She was very beautiful. She took care of the king and served him, but the king did not have sexual relations with her.

decisions.choice: did not know her: had no sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: To "know" a woman is a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual relations (Genesis 4:1; 1 Samuel 1:19). The narrator says plainly that Abishag became the king's nurse and servant, not his wife in the full sense.

decisions.choice: caretaker: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The same rare word as in verse 2: a woman who tends and looks after him.

decisions.choice: the king did not know her: a sign of his weakness, and of Abishag's standing
decisions.reason: In a story about who will rule, the remark shows how weak David has become. It also explains her position later: she lived as part of the king's household but was not his wife (2:17-22).

decisions.choice: know
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וַאֲדֹנִיָּ֧ה בֶן־חַגִּ֛ית מִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י אֶמְלֹ֑ךְ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ ל֗וֹ רֶ֚כֶב וּפָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And Adonijah son of Haggith [was] lifting himself up, saying, I will reign; and he made for himself chariot and horsemen, and fifty men running before him.

en.L: And Adonijah son of Haggith [was] exalting himself, saying, "I will reign." And he made for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men running before him.
en.B: Now Adonijah son of Haggith was putting himself forward, saying, "I will be king." He got himself chariots and horsemen, with fifty men to run ahead of him.
en.R: Meanwhile Adonijah, the son of David's wife Haggith, was boasting, "I am going to be king!" He got chariots and horsemen for himself, and fifty men to run in front of him.

decisions.choice: Adonijah son of Haggith: David's fourth son, now the eldest living
decisions.reason: Adonijah was born at Hebron (2 Samuel 3:4). Amnon and Absalom, the first and third sons, were dead (2 Samuel 13:28-29; 18:14-15), and Chileab, the second, is not heard of again. So by age Adonijah was next in line.

decisions.choice: exalting himself: an ongoing claim
decisions.reason: The verb describes a continuing action: he was raising himself up, setting himself forward as the heir.

decisions.choice: chariots, horsemen and runners: the display of a would-be king
decisions.reason: Absalom did the same when he reached for the throne (2 Samuel 15:1), and Samuel had warned that a king would have men run before his chariots (1 Samuel 8:11).

decisions.choice: David's wife Haggith
decisions.reason: Readable says who Haggith was.

decisions.choice: chariots
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is singular but stands for chariots as a group.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־עֲצָב֨וֹ אָבִ֤יו מִיָּמָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ כָּ֣כָה עָשִׂ֑יתָ וְגַם־ה֤וּא טֽוֹב־תֹּ֨אַר֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְאֹת֥וֹ יָלְדָ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And not pained him his father from his days, saying, why thus have you done? And also he [was] good of form very, and him she bore after Absalom.

en.L: And his father had not pained him [any of] his days, saying, "Why have you done thus?" And he also [was] very good of form, and she bore him after Absalom.
en.B: His father had never once crossed him by asking, "Why have you done this?" He was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.
en.R: His father David had never scolded him or asked, "Why are you doing that?" Adonijah was also very handsome. He was born after Absalom.

decisions.choice: pained him: crossed or rebuked him
decisions.reason: The verb means to hurt or grieve. Here it means David never upset his son by correcting him. The same lack of discipline is seen with Amnon and Absalom (2 Samuel 13:21; 14:33).

decisions.choice: she bore him: his mother, Haggith
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine with no named subject. It means Adonijah's mother bore him; he was the next son born after Absalom, though to a different mother (2 Samuel 3:3-4).

decisions.choice: very handsome: like Absalom
decisions.reason: Absalom too was praised for his looks (2 Samuel 14:25), as Saul was before him (1 Samuel 9:2). Good looks and a father who let him have his way echo the story of the earlier rebel son.

decisions.choice: crossed him
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain verb for the father's hurting or correcting.

decisions.choice: His father David
decisions.reason: Readable names the father.

source.text: וַיִּהְי֣וּ דְבָרָ֔יו עִ֚ם יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֔ה וְעִ֖ם אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַֽיַּעְזְר֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And were his words with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped after Adonijah.

en.L: And his words were with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped after Adonijah.
en.B: He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave Adonijah their support.
en.R: Adonijah made plans with Joab, the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest, and they agreed to support him.

decisions.choice: his words were with: he conferred with them
decisions.reason: To have one's words with someone is to talk things over with him, to plan together.

decisions.choice: helped after: followed and supported
decisions.reason: "Helped after Adonijah" means they took his side and gave him their help.

decisions.choice: Joab and Abiathar: the army commander and a priest of long standing
decisions.reason: Joab was David's nephew and the commander of his army (2 Samuel 8:16). Abiathar had been with David since Saul's days (1 Samuel 22:20-23) and served with Zadok as priest (2 Samuel 15:24-29). Adonijah had the army and part of the priesthood on his side.

source.text: וְצָד֣וֹק הַ֠כֹּהֵן וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע וְנָתָ֤ן הַנָּבִיא֙ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י וְרֵעִ֔י וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑ד לֹ֥א הָי֖וּ עִם־אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But Zadok the priest and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei and the mighty men who [were] to David not were with Adonijah.

en.L: But Zadok the priest and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei and the mighty men who [belonged] to David were not with Adonijah.
en.B: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei and David's own warriors did not side with Adonijah.
en.R: But others did not join Adonijah. They were Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's own warriors.

decisions.choice: Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet: titles of David's court
decisions.reason: Zadok served as priest beside Abiathar (2 Samuel 8:17; 15:24-29). Benaiah was over the king's foreign guard (2 Samuel 8:18; 23:20-23). Nathan was the prophet who brought God's word to David (2 Samuel 7; 12). Their names and titles are kept as the narrator gives them.

decisions.choice: Shimei and Rei: otherwise unknown men
decisions.reason: Neither man is named elsewhere in this role. This Shimei is probably not Shimei son of Gera, who cursed David (2 Samuel 16:5; 1 Kings 2:8). Some have suggested Rei is not a name, but the Hebrew lists it as one.

decisions.choice: the mighty men who belonged to David: his elite warriors
decisions.reason: These are the famous fighters of David's guard, listed in 2 Samuel 23:8-39.

decisions.choice: warriors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "warriors" for "mighty men", which here names a group of fighters.

source.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח אֲדֹנִיָּ֗הוּ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וּמְרִ֔יא עִ֚ם אֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּחֶ֔לֶת אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֖צֶל עֵ֣ין רֹגֵ֑ל וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת־כָּל־אֶחָיו֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה עַבְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sacrificed Adonijah sheep and cattle and fatlings with [the] stone of the Zoheleth, which [is] beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, sons of the king, and all [the] men of Judah, servants of the king.

en.L: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and cattle and fattened cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which [is] beside En-rogel; and he invited all his brothers, the sons of the king, and all the men of Judah, the servants of the king.
en.B: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle and fattened calves at the Stone of Zoheleth, near En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were the king's officials.
en.R: Adonijah offered sheep, cattle and fat calves as sacrifices at the Stone of Zoheleth, near the spring of En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the other sons of the king. He also invited all the king's officials who came from the tribe of Judah.

decisions.choice: sacrificed: slaughtered animals for a sacrificial feast
decisions.reason: The verb is used of sacrifices that were eaten by the worshipers in a feast. Such a feast marked a new king's rise (1 Samuel 11:15; 2 Samuel 15:12), so this was a public claim to the throne.

decisions.choice: the stone of Zoheleth beside En-rogel: a place just outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: En-rogel was a spring south-east of Jerusalem, where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet (Joshua 15:7; 2 Samuel 17:17). It lay below the city and out of sight of the palace, yet near enough to hear noise from the Gihon spring (verses 40-41). What the stone was is not known; its name may mean "the serpent stone" or "the sliding stone".

decisions.choice: the men of Judah, servants of the king: royal officials from Judah
decisions.reason: Adonijah was born at Hebron in Judah (2 Samuel 3:2-4), and he invited the officials from David's own tribe.

decisions.choice: the king's officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the spring of En-rogel
decisions.reason: Readable says what En-rogel was.

source.text: וְֽאֶת־נָתָן֩ הַנָּבִ֨יא וּבְנָיָ֜הוּ וְאֶת־הַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וְאֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א קָרָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men and Solomon his brother not he invited.

en.L: But Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not invite.
en.B: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or his brother Solomon.
en.R: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, David's warriors, or his brother Solomon.

decisions.choice: the names come first: those left out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the people first and the verb last, stressing who was not invited. They are the people who would stand for Solomon.

decisions.choice: Solomon his brother: his half-brother
decisions.reason: Solomon was David's son by Bathsheba (2 Samuel 12:24), so he and Adonijah had different mothers. Leaving him out shows that Adonijah saw him as a rival.

decisions.choice: David's warriors
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נָתָ֗ן אֶל־בַּת־שֶׁ֤בַע אֵם־שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֣וֹא שָׁמַ֔עַתְּ כִּ֥י מָלַ֖ךְ אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־חַגִּ֑ית וַאֲדֹנֵ֥ינוּ דָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Nathan to Bathsheba [the] mother of Solomon, saying, [is it] not [that] you have heard that has reigned Adonijah son of Haggith, and our lord David not knows?

en.L: And Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know [it]?
en.B: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, without our lord David knowing anything about it?
en.R: Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. He said, "Have you heard? Adonijah, Haggith's son, has made himself king, and our master David does not even know about it!

decisions.choice: has become king: has claimed the kingship and acts as king
decisions.reason: The verb means "to reign, to become king". Adonijah had not been anointed, but his followers were already hailing him as king (verse 25).

decisions.choice: Bathsheba the mother of Solomon
decisions.reason: Bathsheba had been the wife of Uriah, and her son Solomon was born after David married her (2 Samuel 11:3, 27; 12:24). The narrator calls her by her tie to Solomon, the son whose life is at stake.

decisions.choice: son of Haggith: set against "mother of Solomon"
decisions.reason: The two princes are named by their mothers, which marks the rivalry between them.

decisions.choice: has made himself king
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Adonijah took the kingship for himself, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: our master David
decisions.reason: Readable says "master" for "lord" where it is not the full title "my lord the king".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה לְכִ֛י אִיעָצֵ֥ךְ נָ֖א עֵצָ֑ה וּמַלְּטִי֙ אֶת־נַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ וְאֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ בְּנֵ֖ךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now come, let me counsel you, please, counsel, and save your life and the life of your son Solomon.

en.L: And now come, let me counsel you, please, [with] counsel, and save your life and the life of your son Solomon.
en.B: Now come, let me give you some advice, so that you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
en.R: Now let me tell you what to do, so that you can save your life and your son Solomon's life.

decisions.choice: and save: so that you may save
decisions.reason: The second command gives the purpose of the first: follow the advice, and you will save your lives.

decisions.choice: save your life and your son's: a rival's family was in danger
decisions.reason: A new king often put to death those who could claim the throne, together with their families (15:29; 2 Kings 10:6-11; 11:1). Bathsheba says the same in verse 21.

decisions.choice: let me tell you what to do
decisions.reason: Readable says "counsel you ... counsel" in plain words.

source.text: לְכִ֞י וּבֹ֣אִי׀אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וְאָמַ֤רְתְּ אֵלָיו֙ הֲלֹֽא־אַתָּ֞ה אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ נִשְׁבַּ֤עְתָּ לַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בְנֵךְ֙ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרַ֔י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֑י וּמַדּ֖וּעַ מָלַ֥ךְ אֲדֹנִיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Go and enter to the king David and say to him, [did] not you, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, that Solomon your son will reign after me and he will sit on my throne? And why has reigned Adonijah?

en.L: Go and go in to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, "Surely Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne"? Then why has Adonijah become king?'
en.B: Go in to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, "Your son Solomon will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne"? So why has Adonijah become king?'
en.R: Go in to King David and say to him, 'Your Majesty, did you not make a promise to me? You said, "Your son Solomon will be king after me. He will sit on my throne." So why has Adonijah become king?'

decisions.choice: your maidservant: Bathsheba's polite way of speaking of herself
decisions.reason: Bathsheba calls herself the king's *'amah*, his female servant, as a polite way of speaking of herself before him (2 Samuel 14:12, 15). It is the language of respect at court, not a statement about her rank.

decisions.choice: the oath to Bathsheba: a promise not told earlier
decisions.reason: The books of Samuel do not record this oath. They tell that the LORD loved Solomon (2 Samuel 12:24-25), and 1 Chronicles 22:9-10 tells of a promise about him. David does not deny the oath in verse 30.

decisions.choice: surely: the word that opens the words of an oath

decisions.choice: waiting for you to tell them
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the link plain.

decisions.choice: who will be king after you

decisions.choice: and it will be: otherwise
decisions.reason: The sentence states what will follow if the king does not act.

decisions.choice: lies down with his fathers (Literal); rests with his ancestors (Balanced); dies (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the death formula in Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: Otherwise (Balanced); If you do not (Readable); treated as
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the condition and the sense of "offenders" plain.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the army: Joab and his officers

decisions.choice: Long live King Adonijah!

decisions.choice: went down to En-rogel
decisions.reason: Readable names the place, from verse 9.

decisions.choice: a man of worth: a reliable, worthy man
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a strong or brave man, or a man of good character. Here it means a trustworthy man, the kind who brings good news (compare 2 Samuel 18:27). Solomon uses a related phrase in verse 52.

decisions.choice: Jonathan son of Abiathar: a messenger before
decisions.reason: Jonathan had carried news for David when Absalom rebelled (2 Samuel 15:36; 17:17-21).

decisions.choice: you bring good news: Adonijah's hope
decisions.reason: The verb form looks forward: Adonijah expects good news, but the news is the opposite.

decisions.choice: you must be bringing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that this is what Adonijah expects.

decisions.choice: Joab
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן֙ יוֹנָתָ֔ן וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ אֲבָ֕ל אֲדֹנֵ֥ינוּ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־דָּוִ֖ד הִמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Jonathan and said to Adonijah, no! Our lord the king David has made king Solomon.

en.L: And Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, "No! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
en.B: Jonathan answered Adonijah, "Not at all! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
en.R: Jonathan answered Adonijah, "No, it is not good news! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.

decisions.choice: No!: the opposite is true
decisions.reason: The word sets what follows against what has just been said: far from good news, the news is bad for Adonijah.

decisions.choice: Our lord King David has made Solomon king: the news in one sentence
decisions.reason: Jonathan states the whole matter first, then gives the details in verses 44-48.

decisions.choice: No, it is not good news!
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "No" answers.

records.literal_gloss: And sent with him the king Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they made him ride on [the] mule of the king.

en.L: And the king has sent with him Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they have made him ride on the king's mule.
en.B: The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they had him ride on the king's mule.
en.R: The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites with Solomon. They put Solomon on the king's own mule.

decisions.choice: the report repeats what happened
decisions.reason: Jonathan's account follows verse 38 almost word for word, so that Adonijah hears each step of what was done.

decisions.choice: the Cherethites and the Pelethites: as in verse 38
decisions.reason: As in verse 38.

decisions.choice: with Solomon; put Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable names Solomon for the pronouns.

source.text: וַיִּמְשְׁח֣וּ אֹת֡וֹ צָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֣ן וְנָתָן֩ הַנָּבִ֨יא לְמֶ֜לֶךְ בְּגִח֗וֹן וַיַּעֲל֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ שְׂמֵחִ֔ים וַתֵּהֹ֖ם הַקִּרְיָ֑ה ה֥וּא הַקּ֖וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁמַעְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And anointed him Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet as king in Gihon, and they went up from there rejoicing, and roared the city; that [is] the sound that you heard.

en.L: And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him as king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That [is] the sound that you have heard.
en.B: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon. From there they have come up rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard.
en.R: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet poured oil on his head at the Gihon spring to make him king. Then they went back up to the city, celebrating. The whole city is excited. That is the noise you heard.

decisions.choice: in an uproar: stirred and noisy
decisions.reason: The verb describes a crowd in loud commotion. It is the same root as Joab's question in verse 41.

decisions.choice: that is the sound you heard: the answer to Joab
decisions.reason: Jonathan ends this part of his report by answering Joab's question.

decisions.choice: poured oil on his head ... to make him king
decisions.reason: As in verse 34.

source.text: וְגַם֙ יָשַׁ֣ב שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה עַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also sat Solomon on [the] throne of the kingdom.

en.L: And also Solomon has sat on the throne of the kingdom.
en.B: What is more, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.
en.R: And Solomon is already sitting on the king's throne.

decisions.choice: and also: the report builds
decisions.reason: Each new part of Jonathan's report begins "and also" (verses 46, 47, 48), each worse for Adonijah.

decisions.choice: the throne of the kingdom: the royal throne
decisions.reason: To sit on it is to reign (verse 35).

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of "and also" with "already".

source.text: וְגַם־בָּ֜אוּ עַבְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לְ֠בָרֵךְ אֶת־אֲדֹנֵ֜ינוּ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֮ לֵאמֹר֒ יֵיטֵ֨ב אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־שֵׁ֤ם שְׁלֹמֹה֙ מִשְּׁמֶ֔ךָ וִֽיגַדֵּ֥ל אֶת־כִּסְא֖וֹ מִכִּסְאֶ֑ךָ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And also came [the] servants of the king to bless our lord the king David, saying, may make good God [the] name of Solomon more than your name, and may he make great his throne more than your throne. And bowed down the king on the bed.

en.L: And also the servants of the king have come to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May God make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne!' And the king bowed down on the bed.
en.B: Besides that, the king's officials have come to congratulate our lord King David, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name more famous than yours, and his throne greater than yours!' And the king bowed in worship on his bed.
en.R: The king's officials have also come to congratulate our lord King David. They said, 'May God make Solomon even more famous than you are! May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} make Solomon's kingdom even greater than yours!' And King David bowed down in worship on his bed.

decisions.choice: God (the Hebrew text as read)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew as written has "your God"; the reading tradition has "God". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: bless: greet with good wishes, congratulate
decisions.reason: To "bless" a person can mean to greet him with good wishes, here to congratulate the king on the choice of his heir.

decisions.choice: make his name better: make him more famous
decisions.reason: A person's "name" is his fame and reputation (2 Samuel 7:9).

decisions.choice: bowed on the bed: worship from his sickbed
decisions.reason: Too weak to rise, the old king bows where he lies, in thanks to God (verse 48), as Jacob did (Genesis 47:31).

decisions.choice: the king's officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: congratulate
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "bless" means here.

decisions.choice: in worship
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the bowing was, from verse 48.

source.text: וְגַם־כָּ֖כָה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בָּר֨וּךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֥ן הַיּ֛וֹם יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֖י וְעֵינַ֥י רֹאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And also thus said the king, blessed [be] Yahweh God of Israel, who has given the day [one] sitting on my throne, and my eyes [are] seeing.

en.L: And also thus the king said, 'Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who has given this day [one] sitting on my throne, and my eyes [are] seeing [it].'"
en.B: And the king also said this: 'Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who has today given me one to sit on my throne, and has let me see it with my own eyes.'"
en.R: And the king said, 'Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! Today {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has put one of my sons on my throne, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has let me live to see it.'"

decisions.choice: blessed be Yahweh: praise and thanks to God
decisions.reason: To "bless" God is to praise and thank him for what he has done (1 Samuel 25:32). David gives God the credit for Solomon's rise.

decisions.choice: one sitting on my throne
alternatives: one of my offspring sitting on my throne
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "one sitting on my throne". The early Greek translation reads "one of my offspring sitting on my throne", which says plainly what the Hebrew implies.

decisions.choice: my eyes are seeing: I have lived to see it
decisions.reason: David is glad to see his heir on the throne in his own lifetime.

decisions.choice: one of my sons
decisions.reason: Readable says who the one on the throne is, as the context makes clear.

decisions.choice: Praise
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel 25:32, Readable says "Praise" for "Blessed be".

source.text: וַיֶּֽחֶרְדוּ֙ וַיָּקֻ֔מוּ כָּל־הַ֨קְּרֻאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְדַרְכּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And trembled and rose all the invited who [were] to Adonijah, and they went each to his way.

en.L: And all the guests who [were] with Adonijah trembled and rose up, and they went each on his way.
en.B: Then all Adonijah's guests got up in alarm, and each of them went his own way.
en.R: All of Adonijah's guests were terrified. They got up and left, each one going his own way.

decisions.choice: trembled and rose: they left in fear
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe a sudden, frightened break-up of the feast.

decisions.choice: each went his way: the party broke up
decisions.reason: Adonijah's supporters scatter so as not to be seen as rebels against the new king.

source.text: וַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ יָרֵ֖א מִפְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Adonijah feared from before Solomon, and he rose and went and took hold of [the] horns of the altar.

en.L: And Adonijah was afraid because of Solomon, and he rose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
en.B: Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, so he got up, went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
en.R: Adonijah was afraid of what Solomon would do to him. So he went and held on to the corners of the altar that stick up like horns.

decisions.choice: took hold of the horns of the altar: seeking safety at God's altar
decisions.reason: The horns were the raised corners of the altar. A man who held on to the altar put himself under God's protection; the law gave that protection only to one who had not killed on purpose (Exodus 21:13-14; compare 2:28-34).

decisions.choice: afraid because of Solomon: afraid of what Solomon would do
decisions.reason: Adonijah knows that his claim has made him the new king's rival (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the corners of the altar that stick up like horns
decisions.reason: Readable explains the "horns", as in Exodus 29:12.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֤ד לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּה֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ יָרֵ֖א אֶת־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְ֠הִנֵּה אָחַ֞ז בְּקַרְנ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשָּֽׁבַֽע־לִ֤י כַיּוֹם֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אִם־יָמִ֥ית אֶת־עַבְדּ֖וֹ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Solomon, saying, look, Adonijah fears the king Solomon, and look, he has taken hold of [the] horns of the altar, saying, let swear to me as the day the king Solomon, if he will kill his servant with the sword.

en.L: And it was told to Solomon, saying, "Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon, and look, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me first, this day, that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
en.B: Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. He has taken hold of the horns of the altar and is saying, 'Let King Solomon first swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
en.R: Someone told Solomon, "Adonijah is afraid of you, King Solomon. He is holding on to the horns of the altar. He says, 'First King Solomon must promise me today that he will not kill me, his servant, with the sword.'"

decisions.choice: as the day: first, this very day
decisions.reason: The phrase means "now, before anything else" (Genesis 25:31, 33). Adonijah will not let go of the altar until he has the oath.

decisions.choice: not kill: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the oath is worded "if he will kill", with the curse on breaking it left unsaid. It means a promise not to kill.

decisions.choice: his servant: Adonijah now calls himself Solomon's servant
decisions.reason: The man who said "I will be king" (verse 5) now speaks of himself as the king's servant, a sign of his submission.

decisions.choice: his servant
decisions.reason: The polite "servant" is kept at every level; Readable adds "me" so the reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: not
decisions.reason: Every level gives the oath's meaning, "will not", rather than the bare "if".

decisions.choice: afraid of you, King Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable addresses Solomon directly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אִ֚ם יִהְיֶ֣ה לְבֶן־חַ֔יִל לֹֽא־יִפֹּ֥ל מִשַּׂעֲרָת֖וֹ אָ֑רְצָה וְאִם־רָעָ֥ה תִמָּצֵא־ב֖וֹ וָמֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Solomon, if he will be as a son of worth, not will fall of his hair to the ground; but if evil is found in him, then he will die.

en.L: And Solomon said, "If he will be a man of worth, not [one] of his hairs will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he will die."
en.B: Solomon said, "If he proves to be a worthy man, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. But if any wrong is found in him, he will die."
en.R: Solomon answered, "If he shows that he is loyal, not one hair on his head will be harmed. But if he does anything wrong, he will die."

decisions.choice: a man of worth: one who proves loyal and upright
decisions.reason: The phrase is close to the one Adonijah used of Jonathan in verse 42. Here it means a man who behaves well toward the king, a loyal subject.

decisions.choice: not one of his hairs will fall to the ground: he will not be harmed at all
decisions.reason: The same saying promises complete safety in 1 Samuel 14:45 and 2 Samuel 14:11.

decisions.choice: if evil is found in him: a condition with a warning
decisions.reason: Solomon's promise is conditional. The story of 2:13-25 shows the condition being tested.

decisions.choice: loyal
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "man of worth" in this setting.

decisions.choice: will be harmed
decisions.reason: Readable explains the saying.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וַיֹּרִדֻ֨הוּ֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ל֥וֹ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְבֵיתֶֽךָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Solomon, and they brought him down from on the altar, and he came and bowed down to the king Solomon; and said to him Solomon, go to your house.

en.L: And King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar; and he came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
en.B: Then King Solomon sent men to bring him down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed before King Solomon, and Solomon told him, "Go home."
en.R: So King Solomon sent some men, and they brought Adonijah down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed down in front of King Solomon. Solomon told him, "Go home."

decisions.choice: brought him down from the altar: led away from it
decisions.reason: The altar stood above the ground, perhaps with steps or a ramp, so Adonijah was brought down from it.

decisions.choice: go to your house: you are spared, but dismissed
decisions.reason: Solomon lets Adonijah live, but sends him away from the court and from any share in power.

decisions.choice: bowed down to King Solomon: Adonijah submits
decisions.reason: By bowing, Adonijah accepts Solomon as king.

decisions.choice: sent men (Balanced); sent some men (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the object of "sent".
